Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

Against the booked optimal of 14.00 km (trip_record, EV-TRIP-02806) the excess is 0.84 km, i.e. 6.00% of optimal (derived.deviation on EV-GPS-02806). POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is BOTH greater than 20% of optimal (here 2.80 km) AND greater than 0.8 km absolute. The absolute limb passes at 0.84 km, but the percentage limb fails by a wide margin, and the two limbs are conjunctive. No deviation is established. Draft 2 - sampled
The disputed trip is TRP-02806, a METERED RYDE_X fare of SGD 21.10. The rider's case is that the route ran 14.84 km instead of the 14.0 km booked optimal, and both advocates agree on the governing figures: the trace distance is 14.84 km (EV-GPS-02806, weight 1.0), the booked optimal is 14.0 km (EV-TRIP-02806, weight 1.0), and the excess is 0.84 km, or 6.00% of optimal. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is BOTH greater than 20% of the optimal distance AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. The absolute limb is cleared (0.84 > 0.8), but the percentage limb is not: 6.00% is far below the 20% the clause requires, and because the two limbs are conjunctive the threshold test fails. The clause then directs that no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The rider is right that the trace figure governs and not the rounded 14.8 km on the trip record — but the point does not help, because on the trace figure the percentage limb still fails, and on the rounded figure the absolute limb would fail as well (exactly 0.80 km, which must exceed 0.8). For the same reason the rider's conditional POL-RD-02 computation (charged_total 21.10, recomputed_fare 20.3920, refund 0.7080, i.e. SGD 0.75 payable) is never reached: POL-RD-02 runs only where a deviation is first established, and it is not.
